relationship.original_equation: LIFO reserve as a fraction of reported inventory = reserve / reported inventory
relationship.locator: Financial Statement Analysis Learning Module 10, Framework for Analyst Adjustments & Adjustments to Inventory, printed pp590–591 (PDF pp604–605), Example 10 and Exhibit 5
relationship.translation_notes: Money divided by money produces a base-one ratio; multiply by 100 only to display a percentage.

variables.source_symbol: LIFO reserve relative to reported inventory
variables.definition: Signed reserve divided by reported inventory, expressed as a base-one fraction
variables.context: Same security, currency, nominal/real basis, timing and period frequency as other quantities in this relationship

assumptions: The reserve and reported inventory are measured at the same date, for the same entity and currency.
Reported inventory is positive; the reserve may be signed.
limitations: The denominator is reported total inventory, which can include non-LIFO inventories; do not confuse this comparison with the share of inventory accounted for under LIFO.
The ratio is not a direct measure of a tax saving or a liquidity ratio.

Example 10 divides the 20,000 reserve by 80,000 labeled current assets (including inventory), yet calls the result a percentage of inventory; the source does not separately give the inventory denominator.
unresolved: No accessible source directly stating this ratio was found after searches for "LIFO reserve percentage of LIFO inventory", "LIFO reserve as a percentage inventory LIFO", and "LIFO reserve divided by LIFO inventory ratio"; the exact comparison was verified only in the owner PDF, which reviewers cannot open. A Wiley curriculum excerpt directly inspected at https://catalogimages.wiley.com/images/db/pdf/9781942471042.excerpt.pdf defines the reserve but does not independently establish this ratio.

Example 10 labels its 80,000 denominator as current assets in Exhibit 5 and as reported inventory in the solution. The actual inventory-only ratio cannot be determined from the disclosed table; the curator-constructed numerical reference is not an owner-example oracle.
